title: LLMs to Support K–12 Teachers in Culturally Relevant Pedagogy: An AI Literacy Example
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge K-12 teachers face in adapting instruction to be culturally relevant, especially in the emerging area of AI literacy. The authors argue that teachers often lack the time, training, and resources needed to meaningfully integrate culturally relevant pedagogy (CRP) into lesson planning, and they explore whether large language models (LLMs) can reduce these barriers.

To investigate this, the paper presents CulturAIEd, an LLM-powered tool that uses student demographic information, a culturally responsive teaching checklist, rubric-based scoring, and just-in-time chatbot support to help teachers adapt AI literacy activities. The study is an exploratory pilot with four K-12 teachers, conducted through 90-120 minute Zoom sessions that included pre-surveys, adaptation tasks, post-surveys, and interviews. Participants modified AI literacy activities around prompt engineering, AI risks, and AI hallucinations, first without guidance, then with a checklist, and finally using CulturAIEd.

The findings suggest that teachers perceived the tool as helpful for identifying opportunities for cultural responsiveness, making culturally responsive modifications, and saving time. Participants reported increased confidence after using the tool and valued the integrated demographics, structured feedback, and coaching-like support. The authors conclude that LLMs may help teachers incorporate CRP into AI literacy instruction more efficiently, but they emphasize that the results are preliminary, based on a very small sample, and should not be treated as causal evidence of effectiveness.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory qualitative-dominant mixed-methods pilot with n=4 and no control group, so it provides low-to-moderate credibility evidence. It is peer-reviewed/archival in format but primarily descriptive rather than causal, with survey and interview data analyzed without inferential testing.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are promising but small and self-reported, centered on teacher perceptions rather than student outcomes. The evidence suggests modest, unclear impact on a priority population (K-12 teachers) rather than demonstrated large effects.

interventions.use_case: LLM-powered teacher support tool (CulturAIEd) for adapting AI literacy activities to culturally relevant pedagogy, combining demographic input, rubric-based feedback, and just-in-time coaching for K-12 lesson planning.

finding.finding_summary: In a qualitative-dominant pilot with n=4 K-12 teachers, CulturAIEd was perceived to reduce the time and effort needed to integrate culturally relevant pedagogy into AI literacy lesson planning. Teachers emphasized streamlined demographic integration, immediate actionable feedback, and reduced planning burden; post-surveys reported all participants at 5/5 confidence in identifying opportunities for cultural responsiveness, up from pre-survey ratings of 3-5/5.
finding.measure: Teacher self-reported confidence, perceived efficiency, and interview themes about planning burden/time savings

finding.finding_summary: The study found improved teacher confidence in culturally responsive design and in identifying opportunities for cultural responsiveness in learning activities after using the LLM tool. This was based on pre/post survey shifts and interview evidence from n=4 teachers, but the study was exploratory and did not report inferential statistics or standardized effect sizes.
finding.measure: Teacher confidence in identifying and implementing culturally responsive modifications
